sections.content:
Looking at the image, the left green (inside the left dark square) now has a white center (W), and the right green (in the protrusion) has a dark gray center (c). So clicking the left green (inside the dark square) swapped the centers: the left green's center changed from c to W, and the right green's center changed from W to c.
This confirms that clicking a green inside a dark square swaps its center with the other green's center.
Now the state is:
- Left green inside left dark square with center W (white)
- Right green in protrusion with center c (dark gray)
- Right dark square empty
Maybe the goal is to have the left green inside the left dark square with center W, and the right green in the protrusion with center c. This is the current state! Let me check if the level completes.
But the level didn't complete after this click. So this is not the solution either.
Let me think about this differently. Maybe the goal is to have both greens inside the same dark square? Or maybe the goal is to have the right green inside the right dark square (which requires finding a way to get it past the purple bar).
Wait, let me reconsider the protrusion. The protrusion is at rows 30-32, and the right dark square is at rows 26-30. The protrusion is BELOW the right dark square. Maybe I need to move the right green UP from the protrusion to get it into the right dark square.
But the right green is at [30-32, 30-32], and the right dark square is at [26-30, 44-48]. The right green is to the left of the right dark square. If I move the right green RIGHT, it would hit the purple bar. If I move it UP, it would go above the protrusion, but the purple bar is at [21-41, 33-38], which covers rows 21-41 and cols 33-38. So the right green at [30-32, 30-32] is to the left of the purple bar (cols 30-32 < 33).
If I move the right green UP, it would go to [28-30, 30-32], which is still to the left of the purple bar. If I keep moving UP, it would eventually go above the protrusion, but the left panel's main body would be above the protrusion.
Actually, the protrusion is a narrow horizontal strip. Above the protrusion is the main body of the left panel. If I move the right green UP from the protrusion, it would enter the main body of the left panel (above the protrusion). Then I could move it RIGHT, but the purple bar would still be in the way.
Hmm, this is getting complicated. Let me try a different approach: maybe I need to move the right green UP from the protrusion, then RIGHT through a gap above the purple bar.
Wait, the purple bar is at [21-41, 33-38]. Above row 21, there's no purple bar. So if I move the right green UP past row 21, I could then move it RIGHT past the purple bar's top edge.
Let me try moving the right green UP multiple times to get it above the purple bar, then RIGHT to get it into the right panel.
